source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָֽטְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after these things, sinned the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker against their lord, against the king of Egypt.

en.L: And it happened after these things [that] the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
en.B: After this, two men in the service of the king of Egypt, his cupbearer and his baker, did wrong against their master.
en.R: After a while, two men who worked for the king of Egypt did something to offend him. One was his cupbearer, who served him his wine. The other was his baker.

es.L: Y sucedió después de estas cosas [que] el copero del rey de Egipto y el panadero ofendieron a su señor, el rey de Egipto.
es.B: Después de esto, dos hombres al servicio del rey de Egipto, su copero y su panadero, cometieron una falta contra su señor.
es.R: Algún tiempo después, dos hombres que trabajaban para el rey de Egipto hicieron algo que lo ofendió. Uno era su copero, el que le servía el vino. El otro era su panadero.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après ces choses, [que] l’échanson du roi d’Égypte et le panetier offensèrent leur seigneur, le roi d’Égypte.
fr.B: Après cela, deux hommes au service du roi d’Égypte, son échanson et son panetier, commirent une faute envers leur maître.
fr.R: Quelque temps plus tard, deux hommes qui travaillaient pour le roi d’Égypte ont fait quelque chose qui l’a offensé. L’un était son échanson, celui qui lui servait son vin. L’autre était son boulanger.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya mambo haya, mnyweshaji wa mfalme wa Misri na mwokaji wakamkosea bwana wao, mfalme wa Misri.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo, watu wawili waliomtumikia mfalme wa Misri, mnyweshaji wake na mwokaji wake, walimkosea bwana wao.
sw.R: Baada ya muda, watu wawili waliomfanyia kazi mfalme wa Misri walifanya jambo lililomchukiza. Mmoja alikuwa mnyweshaji wake, aliyemletea divai yake. Mwingine alikuwa mwokaji wake.

decisions.choice: offended: did wrong against their master
decisions.reason: The verb (chata') is the ordinary word for sin, but between people it means to wrong or offend someone. What the two men did is not told; the point is that they fell out of the king's favor.

decisions.choice: the cupbearer and the baker: officials close to the king
decisions.reason: The cupbearer served the king his wine and was a trusted court officer (Nehemiah 1:11). The baker oversaw the king's bread. Both handled what the king ate and drank, so any suspicion against them was serious.

decisions.choice: his cupbearer, who served him his wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains the office the first time it is named, then keeps the title cupbearer.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B ("offensèrent", "commirent"), passé composé at R ("ont fait")
decisions.reason: As docs/french-style.md section 3: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; Readable uses the passé composé of spoken and school French. Speech, including the dreams the two men recount, is in the passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "le panetier" (L, B); "le boulanger" (R)
decisions.reason: "Panetier" is the French title of the court officer in charge of the bread, the counterpart of "échanson"; Readable uses the everyday "boulanger", as the English Readable says "baker". The chapter keeps each choice throughout.

decisions.choice: "mnyweshaji" (one who gives drink); "mkuu wa wanyweshaji" for the chief cupbearer
decisions.reason: "Mnyweshaji" is formed from "kunywesha", to give to drink, and names the office itself; the baker is "mwokaji", the chief baker "mkuu wa waokaji".

source.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was angry Pharaoh at his two officials, at the chief of the cupbearers and at the chief of the bakers.

en.L: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, with the chief of the cupbearers and with the chief of the bakers.
en.B: Pharaoh's anger was roused against these two officials of his, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
en.R: Pharaoh grew angry at both of these officials of his, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

es.L: Y se enojó el faraón contra sus dos funcionarios, contra el jefe de los coperos y contra el jefe de los panaderos.
es.B: El faraón se enfureció con aquellos dos funcionarios suyos, el jefe de los coperos y el jefe de los panaderos.
es.R: El faraón se enojó con los dos: con el jefe de los coperos y con el jefe de los panaderos.

fr.L: Et Pharaon s’irrita contre ses deux officiers, contre le chef des échansons et contre le chef des panetiers.
fr.B: Pharaon se mit en colère contre ces deux officiers de sa cour, le grand échanson et le grand panetier.
fr.R: Pharaon s’est fâché contre ces deux hommes de sa cour, le chef des échansons et le chef des boulangers.

sw.L: Naye Farao akawakasirikia maafisa wake wawili, mkuu wa wanyweshaji na mkuu wa waokaji.
sw.B: Farao akawaghadhibikia maafisa wake hao wawili, mkuu wa wanyweshaji na mkuu wa waokaji.
sw.R: Farao aliwakasirikia sana maafisa wake hao wawili, yaani mkuu wa wanyweshaji na mkuu wa waokaji.

decisions.choice: his officials ... the chief of the cupbearers: senior court officers
decisions.reason: The word for "officials" (saris) is the title used of Potiphar (39:1). Each man was head over others who did the same work.

decisions.choice: "le grand échanson", "le grand panetier" (B)
alternatives: "le chef des échansons", "le chef des panetiers" (L, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the usual French court titles for the head of each service; Literal keeps the Hebrew "chief of the cupbearers" and Readable the plainer "chef des échansons", "chef des boulangers".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖יםאֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put them in custody [in] the house of the commander of the bodyguards, into the house of the prison, the place where Joseph [was] imprisoned there.

en.L: And he put them in custody in the house of the commander of the guard, in the prison house, the place where Joseph was confined.
en.B: He placed them under guard at the house of the commander of the guard, in the very prison where Joseph was being held.
en.R: He had them locked up in the house of the commander of the guard. Joseph was a prisoner in that same place.

es.L: Y los puso bajo custodia en la casa del jefe de la guardia, en la cárcel, el lugar donde José estaba preso.
es.B: Los mandó poner bajo guardia en la casa del jefe de la guardia, en la misma cárcel donde estaba detenido José.
es.R: Hizo que los encerraran en la casa del jefe de la guardia. José estaba preso en ese mismo lugar.

fr.L: Et il les mit sous garde dans la maison du chef des gardes, dans la maison de la prison, le lieu où Joseph était enfermé.
fr.B: Il les fit garder dans la maison du chef des gardes, dans la prison même où Joseph était détenu.
fr.R: Il les a fait enfermer dans la maison du chef des gardes. Joseph était prisonnier au même endroit.

sw.L: Akawaweka kizuizini katika nyumba ya mkuu wa walinzi, katika nyumba ya gereza, mahali ambapo Yusufu alikuwa amefungwa.
sw.B: Akawaweka chini ya ulinzi katika nyumba ya mkuu wa walinzi, katika gereza lile lile alimokuwa amefungwa Yusufu.
sw.R: Aliamuru wafungwe katika nyumba ya mkuu wa walinzi. Yusufu naye alikuwa mfungwa mahali hapo hapo.

decisions.choice: the commander of the guard: Joseph's master
decisions.reason: The title is the one given to Potiphar (37:36; 39:1), and the prison is in his house. The narrator does not say whether he still held this office or how he now regarded Joseph.

source.text: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ יָמִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And appointed the commander of the bodyguards Joseph with them, and he served them; and they were days in custody.

en.L: And the commander of the guard appointed Joseph [to be] with them, and he attended them; and they were [some] days in custody.
en.B: The commander of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and he waited on them. They remained in custody for some time.
en.R: The commander of the guard gave Joseph the job of serving them, and Joseph looked after them. They were locked up there for some time.

es.L: Y el jefe de la guardia designó a José [para estar] con ellos, y él los atendía; y estuvieron [algunos] días bajo custodia.
es.B: El jefe de la guardia puso a José a su servicio, y él los atendía. Así pasaron un tiempo detenidos.
es.R: El jefe de la guardia le dio a José el trabajo de servirles, y José los cuidaba. Estuvieron presos allí bastante tiempo.

fr.L: Et le chef des gardes plaça Joseph auprès d’eux, et il les servait ; et ils furent [quelques] jours sous garde.
fr.B: Le chef des gardes mit Joseph à leur service, et il s’occupait d’eux. Ils restèrent un certain temps en détention.
fr.R: Le chef des gardes a chargé Joseph de les servir, et Joseph s’est occupé d’eux. Ils sont restés enfermés là un bon moment.

sw.L: Naye mkuu wa walinzi akamweka Yusufu pamoja nao, naye akawahudumia; nao wakawa kizuizini siku [kadhaa].
sw.B: Mkuu wa walinzi akamkabidhi Yusufu kazi ya kuwa pamoja nao, naye akawahudumia. Wakakaa kizuizini kwa muda.
sw.R: Mkuu wa walinzi alimpa Yusufu kazi ya kuwahudumia, naye Yusufu akawatunza. Walikaa gerezani huko kwa muda fulani.

decisions.choice: appointed Joseph with them: Joseph was put in their service
decisions.reason: Joseph is assigned to attend these two high officials, as he had served his master (39:4, the same verb). It also means he is the one who sees them each morning (verse 6).

decisions.choice: days: some time
decisions.reason: "Days" without a number means an indefinite time, perhaps a long one.

source.text: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they dreamed a dream, both of them, each his dream, in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker who [belonged] to the king of Egypt, who [were] imprisoned in the house of the prison.

en.L: And they both dreamed a dream, each his own dream, in one night, each [dream] with its own interpretation, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt who were confined in the prison house.
en.B: Then, on the same night, both prisoners dreamed, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and his baker. Each had his own dream, and each dream called for its own interpretation.
en.R: One night the king's cupbearer and baker both had dreams in prison. Their dreams were different, and each one meant something different.

es.L: Y soñaron un sueño ambos, cada uno su sueño, en una [misma] noche, cada uno según la interpretación de su sueño, el copero y el panadero del rey de Egipto, que estaban presos en la cárcel.
es.B: Entonces, en una misma noche, los dos presos tuvieron un sueño, el copero y el panadero del rey de Egipto. Cada uno tuvo su propio sueño, y cada sueño tenía su propia interpretación.
es.R: Una noche, el copero y el panadero del rey tuvieron sueños en la cárcel. Sus sueños eran distintos, y cada uno quería decir algo diferente.

fr.L: Et ils firent un rêve tous les deux, chacun son rêve, en une [même] nuit, chacun selon l’interprétation de son rêve, l’échanson et le panetier du roi d’Égypte, qui étaient enfermés dans la maison de la prison.
fr.B: Or, la même nuit, les deux prisonniers, l’échanson et le panetier du roi d’Égypte, firent chacun un rêve. Chacun eut son propre rêve, et chaque rêve demandait sa propre interprétation.
fr.R: Une nuit, l’échanson et le boulanger du roi ont fait chacun un rêve dans la prison. Leurs rêves étaient différents, et chacun avait un sens différent.

sw.L: Nao wakaota ndoto wote wawili, kila mmoja ndoto yake, katika usiku mmoja, kila mmoja kulingana na tafsiri ya ndoto yake, mnyweshaji na mwokaji wa mfalme wa Misri, waliokuwa wamefungwa katika nyumba ya gereza.
sw.B: Kisha, usiku mmoja, wafungwa wote wawili, mnyweshaji na mwokaji wa mfalme wa Misri, wakaota ndoto. Kila mmoja aliota ndoto yake mwenyewe, na kila ndoto ilikuwa na tafsiri yake.
sw.R: Usiku mmoja mnyweshaji na mwokaji wa mfalme waliota ndoto wakiwa gerezani. Ndoto zao zilikuwa tofauti, na kila moja ilikuwa na maana yake.

decisions.choice: each according to the interpretation of his dream: each dream fit its own meaning
decisions.reason: The phrase says that each dream carried a meaning of its own, which would come true in its own way. The two dreams look alike but end very differently.

decisions.choice: they dreamed in one night: dreams come in pairs
decisions.reason: As with Joseph's own dreams (37:5-10) and Pharaoh's (41:1-7), the dreams come as a pair. In Genesis such dreams are a way God makes known what is coming.

decisions.choice: "un rêve" at every level
decisions.reason: "Songe" is the older literary word for a dream sent with a meaning; "rêve" is the ordinary modern word, and the Hebrew uses the ordinary word for a dream.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And came to them Joseph in the morning and saw them, and behold, they [were] dejected.

en.L: And Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and look, they [were] downcast.
en.B: Joseph came in to them the next morning and could see how troubled they looked.
en.R: Joseph came to them in the morning, and he saw that something was bothering them.

es.L: Y vino José a ellos por la mañana y los vio, y he aquí que [estaban] abatidos.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, José entró adonde estaban ellos y notó lo preocupados que se veían.
es.R: Por la mañana José fue a verlos, y vio que algo les pasaba.

fr.L: Et Joseph vint vers eux le matin et les vit, et voici, ils [étaient] abattus.
fr.B: Le lendemain matin, Joseph entra chez eux et vit bien qu’ils étaient soucieux.
fr.R: Le matin, Joseph est venu les voir, et il a remarqué que quelque chose les tracassait.

sw.L: Yusufu akaja kwao asubuhi, akawaona, na tazama, [walikuwa] wamesononeka.
sw.B: Asubuhi yake Yusufu akaingia kwao, akaona jinsi walivyokuwa na huzuni.
sw.R: Asubuhi Yusufu alikuja kwao, akaona kwamba kuna jambo lililokuwa likiwasumbua.

decisions.choice: downcast: troubled, out of sorts
decisions.reason: The word (zo'afim) describes a troubled or sullen look; it can also mean vexed or angry.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he asked the officials of Pharaoh who [were] with him in the custody of the house of his master, saying, why [are] your faces bad today?

en.L: And he asked Pharaoh's officials who [were] with him in custody in his master's house, saying, "Why [are] your faces sad today?"
en.B: He questioned the two officials of Pharaoh who were confined with him in his master's house: "Why are your faces so gloomy today?"
en.R: These officials of Pharaoh were prisoners with Joseph in his master's house. He asked them, "Why do you both look so unhappy today?"

es.L: Y preguntó a los funcionarios del faraón que [estaban] con él bajo custodia en la casa de su señor, diciendo: «¿Por qué [están] {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} rostros tristes hoy?».
es.B: Preguntó a los dos funcionarios del faraón que estaban detenidos con él en la casa de su amo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} hoy una cara tan sombría?».
es.R: Estos funcionarios del faraón estaban presos con José en la casa de su amo. Él les preguntó: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:se ven|os veis}} tan tristes hoy?».

fr.L: Et il interrogea les officiers de Pharaon qui [étaient] avec lui sous garde dans la maison de son maître, disant : « Pourquoi vos visages [sont-ils] tristes aujourd’hui ? »
fr.B: Il questionna les deux officiers de Pharaon détenus avec lui dans la maison de son maître : « Pourquoi avez-vous la mine si sombre aujourd’hui ? »
fr.R: Ces officiers de Pharaon étaient prisonniers avec Joseph dans la maison de son maître. Il leur a demandé : « Pourquoi avez-vous l’air si malheureux aujourd’hui ? »

sw.L: Akawauliza maafisa wa Farao waliokuwa pamoja naye kizuizini katika nyumba ya bwana wake, akisema, "Kwa nini nyuso zenu [zina] huzuni leo?"
sw.B: Akawauliza wale maafisa wawili wa Farao waliokuwa wamefungwa pamoja naye katika nyumba ya bwana wake, "Mbona leo nyuso zenu zimejaa huzuni hivi?"
sw.R: Maafisa hao wa Farao walikuwa wafungwa pamoja na Yusufu katika nyumba ya bwana wake. Akawauliza, "Kwa nini nyote wawili mnaonekana na huzuni sana leo?"

decisions.choice: why are your faces bad?: why do you look so unhappy?
decisions.reason: A "bad" face is a sad or troubled one (compare Nehemiah 2:2). Joseph, himself a prisoner, notices the trouble of others.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים סַפְּרוּ־נָ֖א לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, a dream we have dreamed, and [one who] interprets there is not of it. And said to them Joseph, [do] not to God [belong] interpretations? Recount [it], please, to me.

en.L: And they said to him, "We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." And Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell [it] to me."
en.B: "Each of us has had a dream," they replied, "and we have no one to interpret them." Joseph said, "Is it not God who gives interpretations? Please, tell me about them."
en.R: They said, "We had dreams, and there is nobody here who knows what they mean." Joseph answered, "It is God who gives the meaning of dreams. Tell me what you dreamed."

es.L: Y le dijeron: «Hemos soñado un sueño, y no hay quien lo interprete». Y les dijo José: «¿No [pertenecen] a Dios las interpretaciones? {{plural_you:Cuéntenmelo|Contádmelo}}, por favor».
es.B: «Cada uno de nosotros ha tenido un sueño —respondieron—, y no tenemos a nadie que nos los interprete». José les dijo: «¿Acaso no es Dios quien da las interpretaciones? Por favor, {{plural_you:cuéntenmelos|contádmelos}}».
es.R: Ellos le dijeron: «Tuvimos sueños, y aquí no hay nadie que sepa lo que significan». José les contestó: «Es Dios quien da el significado de los sueños. {{plural_you:Cuéntenme|Contadme}} lo que {{plural_you:soñaron|soñasteis}}».

fr.L: Et ils lui dirent : « Nous avons fait un rêve, et il n’y a personne pour l’interpréter. » Et Joseph leur dit : « N’est-ce pas à Dieu [qu’appartiennent] les interprétations ? Racontez-moi [cela], je vous prie. »
fr.B: « Chacun de nous a fait un rêve, répondirent-ils, et nous n’avons personne pour les interpréter. » Joseph leur dit : « N’est-ce pas Dieu qui donne les interprétations ? Racontez-les-moi, je vous en prie. »
fr.R: Ils lui ont dit : « Nous avons fait des rêves, et ici, personne ne peut nous dire ce qu’ils signifient. » Joseph leur a répondu : « C’est Dieu qui donne le sens des rêves. Racontez-moi ce que vous avez rêvé. »

sw.L: Wakamwambia, "Tumeota ndoto, wala hakuna mtu wa kuifasiri." Yusufu akawaambia, "Je, tafsiri si [mali] ya Mungu? Tafadhali niambieni [ndoto hiyo]."
sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Kila mmoja wetu ameota ndoto, wala hatuna mtu wa kuzifasiri." Yusufu akawaambia, "Je, si Mungu anayetoa tafsiri? Tafadhali, nisimulieni."
sw.R: Wakasema, "Tuliota ndoto, na hapa hakuna mtu anayejua maana yake." Yusufu akajibu, "Mungu ndiye anayetoa maana ya ndoto. Niambieni mlichoota."

decisions.choice: there is no one to interpret it: no expert in prison
decisions.reason: In Egypt the interpretation of dreams was a learned skill, practiced by experts with written dream books (41:8). Shut in prison, the two men had no access to them.

decisions.choice: interpretations belong to God: God gives the meaning
decisions.reason: Joseph claims no skill of his own. He will say the same to Pharaoh (41:16). The word for God here is Elohim, the general word, suited to speaking with Egyptians.

decisions.choice: It is God who gives the meaning of dreams
alternatives: Do not interpretations belong to God?
decisions.reason: Readable turns Joseph's question, which expects the answer yes, into a statement.

source.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And recounted the chief of the cupbearers his dream to Joseph and said to him, in my dream, and behold, a vine [was] before me,

en.L: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said to him, "In my dream, look, a vine [was] before me,
en.B: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, saying, "There I was, dreaming, and before me stood a vine,
en.R: Then the chief cupbearer told Joseph about his dream: "I was dreaming, and there was a grapevine standing before me.

decisions.choice: the cupbearer at work: his dream is about his own task
decisions.reason: In the dream the cupbearer does his old work, handing the king his cup. Pharaoh is named three times, and the cupbearer is active throughout, unlike the baker in his dream (verse 17).

en.L: Within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will put Pharaoh's cup into his hand, according to the former custom when you were his cupbearer.

fr.R: Avant trois jours, Pharaon va te faire sortir de prison et te rendre ton ancien travail. Tu lui donneras sa coupe comme tu le faisais avant.

decisions.choice: lift up your head: restore you to honor
decisions.reason: To lift someone's head is to raise him from a low place, here to release him and give him back his position (compare 2 Kings 25:27). Joseph uses the same words for the baker with a terrible twist (verse 19), and the narrator uses them for both men in verse 20.

decisions.choice: your post: your place or office
decisions.reason: The word (ken) means a stand or base; here it is the position the cupbearer held.

decisions.choice: will bring you out of prison
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom. Balanced keeps it, because the wordplay with verses 19 and 20 depends on it.

en.R: Once you are doing well again, do not forget me. Please be good to me. Tell Pharaoh about me so that I can get out of here.

fr.L: Seulement, souviens-toi de moi quand tout ira bien pour toi, et use, je te prie, de loyauté envers moi, et rappelle-moi au souvenir de Pharaon, et fais-moi sortir de cette maison.

sw.L: Ila unikumbuke mambo yatakapokuendea vizuri, na tafadhali unitendee fadhili, na unitaje mbele ya Farao, na unitoe katika nyumba hii.

sw.R: Mambo yakikuendea vizuri tena, usinisahau. Tafadhali, unitendee mema. Mwambie Farao habari zangu ili niweze kutoka hapa.

decisions.choice: only remember me: an earnest request
decisions.reason: The opening words (ki 'im) here mean "only" or "but surely": Joseph asks one thing in return for the good news.

decisions.choice: show loyalty (hesed): repay kindness with kindness
decisions.reason: Hesed is the faithful kindness that people in a relationship owe one another. Joseph has served the man and brought him good news; he asks to be remembered in return.

decisions.choice: mention me to Pharaoh: bring my case to his notice
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to be remembered. Verse 23 uses the same root: the cupbearer did not remember.

decisions.choice: I was stolen: I was kidnapped
decisions.reason: The verb, doubled for emphasis, means stolen; to steal a person and sell him was a crime punished by death (Exodus 21:16). Joseph tells the truth without naming his brothers.

decisions.choice: the pit: the same word as the cistern
decisions.reason: Joseph calls the prison a bor, the word for the pit his brothers threw him into (37:24). For the second time he is in a pit through no fault of his own.

decisions.choice: the land of the Hebrews: Canaan as Egyptians might know it
decisions.reason: Joseph names his homeland by the name of his people, as an Egyptian would understand it.

decisions.choice: "el pozo", "este pozo" (L, B); "esta cárcel" (R)
decisions.reason: "Pozo" keeps the picture of a pit, the same word (bor) as the cistern Joseph's brothers threw him into (37:24), which a Spanish reader can hear again here; Readable says plainly that he means the prison, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: he saw that he had interpreted favorably: why the baker speaks up
decisions.reason: The baker tells his dream only after hearing good news for the other man. The narrator hints that he was hoping for the same.

fr.B: La corbeille du dessus contenait toutes sortes de pâtisseries pour Pharaon, et les oiseaux venaient y picorer, dans la corbeille posée sur ma tête. »
fr.R: Dans la corbeille du haut, j’avais toutes sortes de choses cuites au four pour Pharaon. Mais des oiseaux venaient sans arrêt les manger dans la corbeille sur ma tête. »

sw.L: na katika kikapu cha juu [kulikuwa na] vyakula vya kila aina vya Farao, kazi ya mwokaji, na ndege walikuwa wakivila kutoka kikapuni juu ya kichwa changu."
sw.B: Kikapu cha juu kilikuwa na kila aina ya vyakula vilivyookwa kwa ajili ya Farao, na ndege wakawa wakividonoa kutoka katika kikapu kilichokuwa kichwani mwangu."
sw.R: Katika kikapu cha juu nilikuwa na kila aina ya vyakula vilivyookwa kwa ajili ya Farao. Lakini ndege walikuwa wakija na kuvila kutoka kikapuni kichwani mwangu."

decisions.choice: the birds were eating: an ill omen
decisions.reason: Unlike the cupbearer, the baker does nothing in his dream. The king's food never reaches the king, and the birds take it, as they will take the baker's flesh (verse 19).

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַן יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Joseph and said, this [is] its interpretation: the three baskets, three days they [are].

en.L: And Joseph answered and said, "This [is] its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
en.B: Joseph replied, "Here is the interpretation: the three baskets stand for three days.
en.R: Joseph answered, "I will explain your dream. The three baskets are three days.

es.L: Y respondió José y dijo: «Esta [es] su interpretación: los tres canastos son tres días.
es.B: José respondió: «Esta es la interpretación: los tres canastos representan tres días.
es.R: José le contestó: «Te voy a explicar tu sueño. Los tres canastos son tres días.

fr.L: Et Joseph répondit et dit : « Voici son interprétation : les trois corbeilles sont trois jours.
fr.B: Joseph répondit : « En voici l’interprétation : les trois corbeilles représentent trois jours.
fr.R: Joseph a répondu : « Je vais t’expliquer ton rêve. Les trois corbeilles, ce sont trois jours.

sw.L: Yusufu akajibu, akasema, "Hii [ndiyo] tafsiri yake: vikapu vitatu ni siku tatu.
sw.B: Yusufu akajibu, "Tafsiri yake ni hii: vile vikapu vitatu vinamaanisha siku tatu.
sw.R: Yusufu akamjibu, "Nitakueleza maana ya ndoto yako. Vikapu vitatu ni siku tatu.

source.text: בְּע֣וֹד׀שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת־בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: In yet three days will lift Pharaoh your head from on you and will hang you on a tree, and will eat the birds your flesh from on you.

en.L: Within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head from you and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from you."
en.B: Three days from now Pharaoh will lift up your head, right off your body, and hang you on a pole, and the birds will eat the flesh from your bones."
en.R: Before three days are over, Pharaoh will take off your head and hang your body on a pole. Birds will come and eat your flesh."

es.L: Dentro de tres días más, el faraón levantará tu cabeza de sobre ti y te colgará en un árbol, y las aves comerán tu carne de sobre ti».
es.B: Dentro de tres días el faraón te levantará la cabeza, separándola de tu cuerpo, y te colgará de un poste, y las aves te arrancarán la carne de los huesos».
es.R: Antes de que pasen tres días, el faraón te cortará la cabeza y colgará tu cuerpo de un poste. Vendrán las aves y se comerán tu carne».

fr.L: D’ici trois jours encore, Pharaon élèvera ta tête de dessus toi et te pendra à un arbre, et les oiseaux mangeront ta chair de dessus toi. »
fr.B: Dans trois jours, Pharaon relèvera ta tête, mais en l’ôtant de ton corps, et il te pendra à un poteau, et les oiseaux mangeront la chair de tes os. »
fr.R: Avant trois jours, Pharaon va te faire couper la tête et pendre ton corps à un poteau. Des oiseaux viendront manger ta chair. »

sw.L: Katika siku tatu tena Farao atakiinua kichwa chako kutoka juu yako, na kukutundika juu ya mti, na ndege watakula nyama yako kutoka juu yako."
sw.B: Baada ya siku tatu Farao atakiinua kichwa chako, akikiondoa mwilini mwako, na kukutundika juu ya nguzo, nao ndege watakula nyama ya mwili wako."
sw.R: Kabla siku tatu hazijaisha, Farao atakukata kichwa na kuutundika mwili wako juu ya nguzo. Ndege watakuja kula nyama yako."

decisions.choice: lift up your head from you: cut off your head
decisions.reason: Joseph begins with the same words he used for the cupbearer (verse 13), but adds "from you": the head will be lifted off. The wordplay turns good news into a sentence of death.

decisions.choice: hang you on a tree: the body put on display
decisions.reason: After execution, a body could be hung on a tree or pole for all to see, a mark of disgrace (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Joshua 10:26). The word 'ets means a tree or a wooden pole.

decisions.choice: a pole
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tree"; Balanced and Readable say "pole", the likely form of a gallows.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹםהֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ׀שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the day, the third, the day of the birth of Pharaoh, and he made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted the head of the chief of the cupbearers and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants.

en.L: And it happened on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his officials, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his officials.
en.B: The third day came, and it was Pharaoh's birthday. He held a banquet for all his officials, and with them all present he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker.
en.R: On the third day it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he held a feast for all the men who served him. With all of them watching, he had the chief cupbearer and the chief baker brought out of prison.

es.L: Y sucedió que al tercer día, el día del nacimiento del faraón, él hizo un banquete para todos sus funcionarios, y levantó la cabeza del jefe de los coperos y la cabeza del jefe de los panaderos en medio de sus funcionarios.
es.B: Llegó el tercer día, que era el cumpleaños del faraón. Él ofreció un banquete a todos sus funcionarios, y en presencia de todos ellos levantó la cabeza del jefe de los coperos y la del jefe de los panaderos.
es.R: Al tercer día era el cumpleaños del faraón, y él dio una fiesta para todos los que le servían. Delante de todos ellos, hizo sacar de la cárcel al jefe de los coperos y al jefe de los panaderos.

fr.L: Et il arriva, le troisième jour, jour de la naissance de Pharaon, qu’il fit un festin pour tous ses officiers, et il éleva la tête du chef des échansons et la tête du chef des panetiers au milieu de ses officiers.
fr.B: Le troisième jour arriva : c’était l’anniversaire de Pharaon. Il donna un banquet pour tous ses officiers et, en présence de tous, il releva la tête du grand échanson et celle du grand panetier.
fr.R: Le troisième jour, c’était l’anniversaire de Pharaon, et il a fait une fête pour tous les hommes à son service. Devant eux tous, il a fait sortir de prison le chef des échansons et le chef des boulangers.

sw.L: Ikawa siku ya tatu, siku ya kuzaliwa kwake Farao, akawafanyia maafisa wake wote karamu, akakiinua kichwa cha mkuu wa wanyweshaji na kichwa cha mkuu wa waokaji kati ya maafisa wake.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu ikafika, nayo ilikuwa siku ya kuzaliwa kwa Farao. Akawaandalia maafisa wake wote karamu, na mbele yao wote akakiinua kichwa cha mkuu wa wanyweshaji na cha mkuu wa waokaji.
sw.R: Siku ya tatu ilikuwa siku ya kuzaliwa kwa Farao, naye akawafanyia karamu watu wote waliomtumikia. Wote wakiwa wanatazama, akaamuru mkuu wa wanyweshaji na mkuu wa waokaji watolewe gerezani.

decisions.choice: lifted up the head of both: called them up to judge their cases
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means that Pharaoh summoned both men and dealt with them before his court. What followed differed (verses 21-22), just as Joseph had said.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's birthday: a day of royal favor and judgment
decisions.reason: The day of a king's birth, or of his coming to the throne, was an occasion for feasting and for decisions about prisoners.

decisions.choice: his servants: his officials
decisions.reason: The "servants" of a king are his courtiers and officers, not slaves.

decisions.choice: had ... brought out of prison
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom here.

source.text: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he restored the chief of the cupbearers to his cupbearing, and he put the cup on the palm of Pharaoh.

en.L: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office of cupbearer, and he placed the cup into Pharaoh's palm.
en.B: He reinstated the chief cupbearer in his office, and the cupbearer went back to placing the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
en.R: Pharaoh let the chief cupbearer serve as cupbearer again. The man went back to handing Pharaoh his wine.

es.L: Y restituyó al jefe de los coperos a su oficio de copero, y él puso la copa en la palma del faraón.
es.B: Al jefe de los coperos lo repuso en su cargo, y este volvió a poner la copa en la mano del faraón.
es.R: El faraón dejó que el jefe de los coperos volviera a ser su copero. El hombre volvió a servirle el vino al faraón.

fr.L: Et il rétablit le chef des échansons dans son office d’échanson, et celui-ci mit la coupe dans la paume de Pharaon.
fr.B: Il rétablit le grand échanson dans sa charge, et celui-ci recommença à mettre la coupe dans la main de Pharaon.
fr.R: Pharaon a permis au chef des échansons de redevenir échanson. L’homme a recommencé à servir son vin à Pharaon.

sw.L: Akamrudisha mkuu wa wanyweshaji kwenye kazi yake ya unyweshaji, naye akakiweka kikombe katika kiganja cha Farao.
sw.B: Akamrudisha mkuu wa wanyweshaji kwenye cheo chake, naye akaendelea kukiweka kikombe mkononi mwa Farao.
sw.R: Farao alimruhusu mkuu wa wanyweshaji kuwa mnyweshaji tena. Mtu huyo akarudi kumletea Farao divai yake.

source.text: וְאֵ֛ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים תָּלָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And the chief of the bakers he hanged, just as had interpreted to them Joseph.

en.L: But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
en.B: The chief baker, though, he hanged, exactly as Joseph had explained to them.
en.R: But on Pharaoh's orders the chief baker was put to death and his body hung on a pole. Things turned out exactly the way Joseph had explained to them.

es.L: Pero al jefe de los panaderos lo colgó, tal como José les había interpretado.
es.B: Al jefe de los panaderos, en cambio, lo colgó, exactamente como José les había explicado.
es.R: Pero por orden del faraón, al jefe de los panaderos lo mataron y colgaron su cuerpo de un poste. Todo sucedió tal como José les había explicado.

fr.L: Mais le chef des panetiers, il le pendit, comme Joseph le leur avait interprété.
fr.B: Quant au grand panetier, il le fit pendre, exactement comme Joseph le leur avait expliqué.
fr.R: Mais sur l’ordre de Pharaon, on a mis à mort le chef des boulangers et on a pendu son corps à un poteau. Tout s’est passé exactement comme Joseph le leur avait expliqué.

sw.L: Lakini mkuu wa waokaji akamtundika, kama vile Yusufu alivyowafasiria.
sw.B: Bali mkuu wa waokaji akamtundika, sawasawa na jinsi Yusufu alivyowaeleza.
sw.R: Lakini kwa amri ya Farao mkuu wa waokaji aliuawa, na mwili wake ukatundikwa juu ya nguzo. Mambo yakawa sawasawa kabisa na jinsi Yusufu alivyowaeleza.

decisions.choice: just as Joseph had interpreted: the interpretation proved true
decisions.reason: Both dreams come true exactly. The God who gives interpretations (verse 8) has spoken through Joseph.

decisions.choice: the chief baker was put to death and his body hung on a pole
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both parts of what Joseph foretold in verse 19.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־זָכַ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not remembered the chief of the cupbearers Joseph, and he forgot him.

en.L: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
en.B: But the chief cupbearer gave no thought to Joseph; he put him out of his mind.
en.R: But the chief cupbearer did not keep Joseph in mind. Joseph slipped from his memory.

es.L: Pero el jefe de los coperos no se acordó de José, sino que lo olvidó.
es.B: Pero el jefe de los coperos no pensó más en José; se lo quitó de la mente.
es.R: Pero el jefe de los coperos no se acordó de José. Se olvidó por completo de él.

fr.L: Et le chef des échansons ne se souvint pas de Joseph, mais il l’oublia.
fr.B: Mais le grand échanson ne pensa plus à Joseph ; il le chassa de son esprit.
fr.R: Mais le chef des échansons n’a pas pensé à Joseph. Il l’a complètement oublié.

sw.L: Lakini mkuu wa wanyweshaji hakumkumbuka Yusufu, bali akamsahau.
sw.B: Lakini mkuu wa wanyweshaji hakumfikiria Yusufu tena; alimwondoa kabisa akilini mwake.
sw.R: Lakini mkuu wa wanyweshaji hakumkumbuka Yusufu. Alimsahau kabisa.

decisions.choice: did not remember ... forgot him: said twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The narrator says it both ways. Joseph had asked to be remembered (verse 14); he stays in prison two more full years (41:1, 9).
